meta.name: DigiDoc Lab Reference Ranges
meta.ordering: Sorted by consensusTier (1 = most standardized, widely agreed ranges and critical limits; 2 = well documented but assay/lab dependent; 3 = specialized or highly method dependent), then clinical category.

sources.ABIM: American Board of Internal Medicine, Laboratory Test Reference Ranges, revised January 2026 (adult reference intervals).
sources.CRIT: Critical (panic) limits harmonized from published lab policies: Labcorp (2020/2024), University of Chicago Medical Center, Akron Children's, Bioreach, Starling labs; where labs differ, the more conservative middle value is used.
sources.PED: Pediatric intervals: UChicago Clinical Labs 2024 (creatinine), ACCP PedSAP/ACSAP tables, ALT pediatric study-protocol tables, plus standard pediatric references (Nelson/Harriet Lane/RCPCH-type tables). Pediatric values are approximate and lab dependent.
sources.ADA: American Diabetes Association Standards of Care (glucose/HbA1c categories).
sources.NCEP: NCEP ATP III lipid categories (also reproduced in ABIM).
sources.KDIGO: KDIGO CKD staging and albuminuria categories.
sources.WHO2021: WHO Laboratory Manual for Semen Examination, 6th ed. (lower reference limits).
sources.IADPSG: IADPSG/WHO gestational diabetes OGTT thresholds (75 g).
sources.CDC: CDC blood lead reference value for children (3.5 µg/dL).
sources.STD: Standard textbook/guideline reference interval; varies more between labs.

howToInterpret: 1. Match the test by any entry in `names` (case-insensitive, ignore punctuation).
2. Convert the reported unit to the primary `unit` using `unitConversions` (primary = alt * multiplyToGetPrimary).
3. Pick the `ranges` entry where sex matches (or 'any'), age in days is within [ageMinDays, ageMaxDays), and `context` matches if given (e.g. pregnancy, morning).
4. If value < criticalLow -> CRITICAL_LOW; > criticalHigh -> CRITICAL_HIGH; else value < low -> LOW; value > high -> HIGH; else NORMAL.
5. If `grades` exist, report the matching grade label (e.g. prediabetes) in addition.
7. Always prefer the reference range printed on the patient's own lab report when it differs; ask for a clearer photo if the unit or value is unreadable.
8. Critical or alertOnHigh='emergency' results must trigger the red emergency screen (rule-based, never LLM-decided).
meta.specialtyDefaultsNote: `specialty` lists are suggestions in priority order; map to doctors in the database by `specialty` column.
meta.disclaimer: Reference intervals vary by laboratory, method, age, sex, pregnancy and population. This data supports report explanation only and is not a diagnosis. Ranges and critical limits have not been reviewed by a licensed physician for clinical use; have a clinician review before any real patient deployment.
